import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1028

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1028](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1028)
- [Er63d] Erdős, Pál, *On combinatorial questions connected with a theorem of Ramsey and van der
  Waerden*. Mat. Lapok (1963), 29-37.
- [Er71] Erdős, P., *Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis*.
  Combinatorial Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [ErSp71] Erdős, P. and Spencer, J., *Imbalances in $k$-colorations*. Networks (1971/72),
  379-385.
-/

open Filter Asymptotics

namespace Erdos1028

/-- The imbalance of a finite set `X` under a colouring `f`, that is,
$\left\lvert \sum_{x<y\in X} f(x,y)\right\rvert$. -/
def imbalance (f : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ) (X : Finset ℕ) : ℤ :=
  |∑ x ∈ X, ∑ y ∈ X.filter (fun y => x < y), f x y|

/-- `H n` is the minimum, over all colourings `f` of pairs from `{1, …, n}` with values in
`{-1, 1}`, of the largest imbalance of a subset `X ⊆ {1, …, n}`. -/
noncomputable def H (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m | ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ, (∀ x y, f x y = 1 ∨ f x y = -1) ∧
    ∀ X ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n, imbalance f X ≤ (m : ℤ)}

/--
Let
$$H(n)=\min_f \max_{X\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}} \left\lvert \sum_{x<y\in X} f(x,y)\right\rvert,$$
where $f$ ranges over all functions $f:\{1,\ldots,n\}^2\to \{-1,1\}$. Estimate $H(n)$.

Erdős [Er63d] proved
$$\frac{n}{4}\leq H(n) \ll n^{3/2}.$$
Erdős and Spencer [ErSp71] proved that $H(n)\gg n^{3/2}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1028.lean"]
theorem erdos_1028 :
    (fun n => (H n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop]
      fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős [Er63d] proved
$$\frac{n}{4}\leq H(n) \ll n^{3/2}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1028.variants.lower_bound :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (n : ℝ) / 4 ≤ (H n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős [Er63d] proved
$$\frac{n}{4}\leq H(n) \ll n^{3/2}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1028.variants.upper_bound :
    (fun n => (H n : ℝ)) ≪ (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős and Spencer [ErSp71] proved that $H(n)\gg n^{3/2}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1028.variants.erdos_spencer :
    (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ (3 / 2 : ℝ)) ≪ (fun n => (H n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1028

reformulations.difference: The primary papers sum over undirected edges; Lean represents these by increasing pairs x < y in an unrestricted integer-valued matrix. The website's x ≠ y notation could misleadingly suggest an ordered-pair sum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: [Er71], Problem 24, explicitly assigns signs for 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n, and [ErSp71], equations (1)–(4), colours two-element subsets. Every such edge has exactly one increasing representative. Assigning {x,y} the value f(min x y)(max x y) makes the Lean sum exactly the edge-colour imbalance, with no factor of two. Conversely, every edge-colouring extends to a matrix; the unused entries cannot affect the sum. A literal nonsymmetric directed-pair reading of the website is not the claim posed in the cited primary literature.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses the natural-number infimum of feasible uniform upper bounds, with globally ±1-valued functions on ℕ × ℕ, rather than an explicit finite minimum of finite maxima over edge-colourings.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The admissible set is nonempty: a constant colouring has a finite maximum imbalance over the powerset of [1,n]. Thus Nat.sInf is an attained minimum, not its empty-set default. All imbalances are nonnegative integers, so the least feasible natural upper bound is exactly the finite minimax value. The scratch file proves, for every n and m, that H n ≤ m iff there is a colouring constrained only on increasing pairs in [1,n] whose every subset imbalance is at most m. Extending that colouring by +1 outside those pairs proves that the global sign constraint adds no restriction.

sources_consulted: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/ and https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html (primary-paper archive and bibliography)

[Er63d] Erdős, On combinatorial questions connected with a theorem of Ramsey and van der Waerden, Mat. Lapok 14 (1963), 29–37; especially pp. 30–31 and 35–36. https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1963-15.pdf
[Er71] Erdős, Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis (1971), 97–109; Problem 24, p. 107, including the note added in proof. https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-25.pdf
[ErSp71] Erdős and Spencer, Imbalances in k-colorations, Networks 1 (1971/72), 379–385; definitions (1)–(4), the theorem, and the k=2 argument. https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-05.pdf
review.notes:
All six declarations were checked; no mathematical defect or stale status was found. The source records SOLVED (LEAN), agreeing with the four research-solved tags. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, independent checks prove admissible-set nonemptiness, the finite-colouring characterization, H(0)=H(1)=0 and H(2)=H(3)=H(5)=1, and equivalence of the main Θ statement to positive two-sided eventual bounds. The file compiles without errors or sorry dependencies. The eventual lower bound appropriately avoids small exceptions, including n=5.

The linked formal-proof artifact states an equivalent finite minimax theorem and contains no explicit sorry or custom axioms. Its original Lean/Mathlib v4.29.1 kernel check was not independently reproduced: compilation under the sandbox's v4.33.1 encountered compatibility errors, which are not evidence of a mathematical or status defect. Direct source-page access was challenged by Cloudflare; the main and LaTeX pages were read through a public rendering service. The forum rendering was unavailable, but the cited primary papers supplied the relevant definitions, bounds, and remarks.
